messages:
Maya: Quick runbook draft for Field Ops — lightweight shared-cache + streaming guidance for low-touch customers. Goal: reduce cold-starts, minimize cost, avoid prefill bloat. Ping @Rory for enablement notes.

Rory: nice. Can we add a one-liner troubleshooting checklist for renewals? e.g., 1) check prefill hit-rate 2) confirm streaming enabled 3) SDK timeouts

Maya: yes. Here's a tight checklist + recommended defaults:
- prefill: only for first 3 requests / user session
- cache scope: account-level prefix cache (TTL 60s)
- batching: max batch size 8 for short latency SLOs
- streaming: enable for sessions < 15s

Devon: test commands we used in dev for telemetry:
```
# check cache hit rate
curl -s "https://console.redwood/api/metrics?m=cache_hit_rate&acc=ACCT_ID"
# toggle streaming
redwoodctl set --account ACCT_ID --streaming true
```

Samir: Add notes on customer messaging for renewals — recommend include: warmup guide, expected latency, upgrading to Dedicated for high-throughput.

Rory: Also add fallback policy snippet: prefer smaller quantized model when GPU contention > 70%.

Maya: capturing feedback loop: create a short survey link we send after go-live, capture token/cost surprises + accuracy regressions. Template: "How did livemode latency compare to staging?" :email:

OncallBot: Deploy succeeded for branch cs/runbook/fieldops at 2025-03-05T14:12Z :white_check_mark:

Maya: thanks all — I'll paste this into the onboarding doc and share a one-pager for AE enablement. Anyone want to pair on a quick run through next Tue? @Rory @Devon :calendar:

Rory: I can do Tue 11am PT.

Devon: +1

Maya: done, will schedule. Final: keeping cache small, prefer streaming for quick UX wins, capture survey + telemetry within 72h of go-live. End of thread.
